findings.title: Resolve the parameter type in the method's scope before replacing it
findings.detail: Complete token spelling still does not establish that the parameter denotes the impl's self type. A method type parameter can shadow a module type with the same name: inside impl S, fn f<S: T>(c: &S) uses the generic S, not the owning struct S. Both spellings pass this comparison. Replacing c with self makes method lookup use the concrete owner's inherent methods instead of the generic bound's trait methods. For the counterexample in evidence, S::f::<S>(&S) remains a valid qualified call, but c.value() becomes self.value(), selecting the inherent value 1 rather than trait value 2. The nominal and overlay checks later in convert_to_method only decide whether to rewrite callers; retaining UFCS cannot undo this declaration/body change. This leaves original comment 4079089186 incompletely repaired and can silently alter runtime behavior despite clean diagnostics.
findings.evidence: Static counterexample, not executed in this review: trait T { fn value(&self) -> u8; } struct S; impl T for S { fn value(&self) -> u8 { 2 } } impl S { fn value(&self) -> u8 { 1 } fn f<S: T>(c: &S) -> u8 { c.value() } } fn main() { println!("{}", S::f::<S>(&S)); }. Terminal semantic output for prod-code def --symbol receiver_for crates/prod-code-mcp/src/to_method/helpers.rs confirms lines 57-59 accept identical S token sequences. Numbered source at crates/prod-code-mcp/src/to_method/rust.rs:71-78 supplies the outer impl spelling without checking the method's type bindings; :86-137 replaces the declaration and resolved c uses. Its identity lookup starts only at :145 and the dispatch proof is conditional on caller rewriting at :207-234. The two versions of the counterexample differ only by fn f<S: T>(&self) and self.value(); the remaining generic argument and qualified caller stay valid.
findings.suggested_fix: Establish the selected parameter referent's resolved type identity, including its generic arguments and binding scopes, against the impl self type before planning declaration or body edits. At minimum refuse owner-name shadowing by method type parameters. Preserve supported exact-owner declarations and successful proved caller conversion; add a focused public conversion regression for this trait-versus-inherent dispatch case during the repair.

findings.title: Locate the selected top-level parameter rather than its first matching text
findings.detail: The new cursor calculation still searches the whole parameter list for target.raw. Valid Rust function-pointer types can contain named arguments, so an earlier parameter such as helper: fn(tax: &Tax) contains the complete raw spelling of the later selected tax: &Tax parameter. list.find therefore selects the function-pointer argument label, not the destination binding. The definition query can still resolve Tax correctly, while the references query targets that unrelated label and omits the actual tax uses. After removing the destination declaration, those uses remain tax. Normal diagnostics reject an otherwise valid move; force can write unresolved identifiers. This is the same selected-declaration failure described by original comment 4088035140, with a longer matching substring than the existing module-word regression covers.
findings.evidence: Static input, not executed in this review: struct Tax(u32); struct Order(u32); impl Order { fn f(&self, helper: fn(tax: &Tax), tax: &Tax) -> u32 { helper(tax); self.0 + tax.0 } } fn helper(_: &Tax) {} fn main() { println!("{}", Order(1).f(helper, &Tax(2))); }. Semantic terminal output for prod-code def --symbol parse_declared crates/prod-code-mcp/src/signature/parse.rs confirms :307-322 splits top-level parameters, selects their names, and stores only raw/name. Numbered source at crates/prod-code-mcp/src/move_method/method.rs:78-91 selects the correct top-level Declared, but :130-141 discards that identity through list.find(&target.raw). With target.raw equal to tax: &Tax, its first occurrence is inside fn(tax: &Tax). The resulting param_at is passed to references at :208-215, and only returned offsets become self markers at :216-262. Existing cursor tests at crates/prod-code-mcp/tests/rust_method_preservation/receiver.rs:59-102 exercise an earlier tax module word, not an earlier occurrence of the whole raw parameter.
findings.suggested_fix: Retain the actual top-level parameter's source range while parsing, or locate the selected index using a balanced top-level parameter scan with offsets. Derive both binding and type cursors from that range, never from list.find(target.raw). Preserve mutable short-name and lifetime behavior and cover an earlier named function-pointer argument with a focused public move regression during the repair.
